paper_id: Dong et al. - 2013 - Fine-Grained Location-Free Planarization in Wireless Sensor Networks
title: Fine-Grained Location-Free Planarization in Wireless Sensor Networks
motivation: Location-based planarization requires costly GPS or NP-hard localization, limiting applicability in large-scale sensor networks.
problem_framing: Extract a connected planar subgraph (TPS) from connectivity graph G with bounded stretch factor, using only local connectivity information.
key_insight: Using underlying representations (underlying paths) enables dynamically transforming non-CDM edges into conflict-free edges, achieving denser sampling than CDM.
method_signature: Construct RWG with underlying representation, compute maximal conflict-free edge set via conflict graph MIS, perform separable conflict resolution.
evaluation_criteria: Planarity guarantee, stretch factor (worst/average), connectivity (number of branches), edge count ratio vs CDM.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Cannot guarantee constant stretch factor for arbitrary inputs, though simple test exists for correctness and simulations show small stretch.
evidence_for_taste: edges not in CDM can often be transformed
CDM will be disconnected and contain many connected components
large distortion of those planar structures
cannot be easily applied in those applications
theoretical result requires the diameter be at least 290
thinking_moves: 先用CDM方法演示其局限性(稀疏采样导致断开)
定义底层表示来捕获边的几何关系而非依赖位置
将冲突检测形式化为图独立集问题
